notes.text: The opening links the six-operation formalism with the definition of homology and an essential relation between the two homological/cohomological terms. The noun before the adjectives remains doubtful. The author lists settings involving quasi-coherent sheaves, topological spaces, étale coefficients, and the interlinear analytic case.

The parenthesis says that this formalism remains to be developed in the crystalline context and, in characteristic 0, for stratified modules with the inserted qualification à singularités, with Hodge structures over the displayed double-stroked C, and finally for motives.

The author explicitly writes je suis persuadé, partout, peut-être, and disons. These are retained as author qualifications, not converted to established conclusions. No question, new date, salutation, closing or signature is visible on this continuation sheet.

The author page number is 7. The lower-left archival pencil number is 152 and appears only as a TeX comment. H’s editorial page number 151 is not manuscript wording. No other page or translation was consulted.

The potentially consequential inspections were the alpha-shaped Lf exponent, separately placed exclamation marks, plain versus doubled R/L, the live underlined coefficient condition, the inserted séparé, and the clipped final characteristic abbreviation. They were palaeographic readings only. No proof, re-proof, computation, formal certificate, or use-and-recheck event took place; checks is therefore empty.

The manuscript has paired upright quotation strokes. H’s guillemets are logged because the brief requires actual quotation shape. Its ell spelling and C’s l spelling refer to the same looped lowercase letter here and are not counted as a separate typeface error. Hyphen/dash TeX width spellings alone are not counted as differences.

Four independent insertion guides are reproduced in TikZ at their local source positions. The semicolon remains in the right guide; the report records the uncertain linear role without relocating or duplicating its ink. The isolated spot below un has no recoverable textual attachment and is documented as a probable copying/stray mark rather than assigned punctuation.
The bottom edge physically removes parts of la, car and all possible following punctuation. This is an image limit. The final comma conjectured by C is not visible and has not been supplied.

coverage: The whole 1680×2365 image was viewed once for layout, followed once each by the supplied 1680×1262 upper and 1680×1263 lower halves, in that order. I read all approximately 25 physical body lines sequentially against the full C and H texts, including every agreed word, ending, accent, abbreviation, punctuation mark and inline mathematical sign. I inspected both page numbers, the two deletions, the live underline, all four interlinear additions and all four associated guides, plus the clipped lower edge. There is no display, mathematical diagram, independent drawing other than the insertion guides, heading, closing or signature on this continuation page. Nine unresolved places or compact local constructions received one crop each; no decided place was re-cropped and no whole half was enlarged again. The split noun has both end-of-line and next-line source boxes. The two sources omit the guide graphics; H additionally differs in the words and states itemised in changes, while the bottom article, accent form and surname require fresh doubt. The semicolon is kept in its physical guide. Ordinary visual reading is not reported as mathematical verification.
